question_text: What public document must all public officials and employees file under oath upon assumption of office and on or before April 30 of every year thereafter?

options.text: Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN)

hint_ladder.title: Think about financial transparency
hint_ladder.text: This question targets a key anti-corruption measure. Think of the document that lists your assets, liabilities, and net worth.

hint_ladder.title: Look for the annual deadline
hint_ladder.text: The clue is 'every year by April 30.' Only one document has this fixed, recurring deadline.

hint_ladder.title: Remember the acronym
hint_ladder.text: This four-letter acronym starts with S and ends with N. It summarizes your financial status under oath.

hint_ladder.title: Match the description exactly
hint_ladder.text: Only SALN requires oath, assumption filing, and yearly update. Others have different timelines or purposes.

A.text: Correct. RA 6713 Sec. 8 requires SALN under oath upon assumption and by April 30 yearly to promote transparency.

B.text: You might have chosen B because PDS is a familiar HR form, but it's not an annual sworn financial disclosure.

C.text: You might have chosen C because IPCR is an official document, but it measures work performance, not wealth.

D.text: You might have chosen D because a certificate sounds like proof, but it's a one-time document, not filed every year.

next_time_rule: Key signal: 'under oath' and 'April 30' point directly to SALN—no other form has that combination.
blueprint_id: RA 6713 Section 8 — Disclosure of Assets and Liabilities (SALN)
deconstruct_text:
Picture this: You're a newly elected Barangay Kagawad. On your first day in office, you must submit a sworn statement of all your ari-arian (assets) and utang (liabilities). That's the SALN under RA 6713 Section 8.

Then every year, on or before April 30, you update it. Kahit maraming trabaho o may paputok sa fiesta, dapat i-file yan! The SALN is your sworn financial report, required para maiwasan ang corruption.

Now, bakit hindi PDS? The Personal Data Sheet is just a basic info form—walang oath, walang annual deadline. Ang IPCR? Performance review 'yan, hindi naka-focus sa pera.

Certificate of Eligibility? One-time proof lang ng exam, hindi annual. So 'pag nakita mo 'under oath' at 'April 30,' SALN agad ang isagot mo.
